title: Sega Rally Championship
japaneseTitle: セガラリーチャンピオンシップ
shortDescription: Sega AM3 and Tetsuya Mizuguchi's legendary arcade rally racer, pioneering surface-friction tire physics across tarmac, gravel, and mud.
historicalSignificance: The seminal masterpiece that established the modern rally racing video game genre, acclaimed for its legendary Toyota Celica GT-Four vs. Lancia Delta HF Integrale rivalry and flawless surface friction handling.

editorialContent.overview: Conceived by producer Tetsuya Mizuguchi and director Kenji Sasaki, Sega Rally Championship debuted on Model 2 arcade boards before receiving one of the most technically celebrated arcade-to-home conversions on the Sega Saturn.
editorialContent.gameplay: Pioneered distinct tire-friction physics according to road surface—cars behave radically differently when sliding from tarmac onto loose gravel or slick mud, guided by a co-driver calling out 'Easy right, maybe!'
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: The Sega Saturn conversion famously achieved a silky locked 30 FPS with peerless analog steering wheel support, pushed as a demonstration of the system's dual processors.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Directly inspired the entire subgenre of rally racing simulations, including the Colin McRae Rally and Dirt franchises.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on Sega Model 2 arcade hardware and Sega Saturn CD-ROMs.

verifiedFactualData.sales: Over 1.2 million copies on Sega Saturn; massive coin-op hit
awards: Crowned Greatest Racing Game of All Time (Retro Gamer Magazine)

technicalSpecs.engine: Sega Model 2A CRX hardware / Custom Saturn Engine
